label: Interpretive principle: if an author states an unrestricted conclusion, presents it as following…
paraphrase: Interpretive principle (project methodology, not a source claim): if an author states an unrestricted conclusion, presents it as following necessarily, words a premise so that it admits a reading on which the conclusion follows, the rival reading does not yield it, and the passage examined for counter-evidence (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, the only one weighed so far) does not force the rival reading, then the reading that yields the conclusion is the intended one.
